# @zakkster/lite-depth v2.0.0

Zero-GC Canvas2D software-projected 3D. Zdog's niche (flat-shaded, painter-sorted
pseudo-3D on a 2D canvas), arena-backed and allocation-free per frame. Single-file
ESM. Node/browser. MIT. Author: Zahary Shinikchiev.

Runtime deps: @zakkster/lite-arena, @zakkster/lite-fastbit32, @zakkster/lite-aabb.
Optional cold-path peers: lite-signal (DI), lite-raf, lite-clock, lite-sprite-cache.

## Model

- A Stage owns an arena of nodes (SoA, generational handles), a pre-allocated
  frame arena, and a Canvas2D ctx. Geometries and materials are registered once
  and referenced by id; nodes instance them.
- stage.frame(dt) runs: transform -> project -> collect+cull -> radix sort ->
  paint. Entirely over pre-allocated storage: 0 alloc/frame. Structural mutation
  (add/remove/reparent) is cold and may allocate.
- Painter's algorithm: no depth buffer. Faces sorted back-to-front by a packed
  Uint32 key: (layer<<26) | quantize26(centroidViewZ + depthBias). Far -> key 0
  (painted first), near -> DEPTH_MAX (painted last).

## Import

    import { createStage, geometry, material, materialFromRamp,
             createCamera, updateCamera, mathKernels, FLAGS, TAU,
             version, LANE_VERSION, FORMAT_VERSION }
      from '@zakkster/lite-depth';
FORMAT_VERSION re-exports @zakkster/lite-aabb's packed-format contract version
(the [minX,minY,maxX,maxY] float32x4 layout the node-box lane + scene-bbox merge
depend on). createStage asserts it === 1 and throws if the peer ever drifts.

## Frozen binary contract (LANE_VERSION)

- LANE_VERSION (currently 1) is the frozen binary-contract version, on a SEPARATE
  axis from `version` -- the two never track each other. LANES.md is the normative
  spec. LANE_VERSION covers: the per-node arena lane set (names + TypedArray
  types), the FLAGS bit assignment, the packKey sort-key layout (6 layer bits << 26
  | 26 depth bits) + the LINEAR-in-viewZ quantize curve, the frame-arena layout +
  the 3 cold draw sentinels (DRAW_STROKE/DRAW_CLIP/DRAW_SHADOW), and the D6 Worker
  wire (23-key transfer set + worldNonUnif). It does NOT cover: stats field values
  or additive stats fields (a minor bump), geometry-store fields, capacity options,
  the packed node-box layout (delegated to lite-aabb FORMAT_VERSION), or Motion.js.
- matEff (the persistent per-node material-override lane) is a MEMBER of the
  per-node lane set but a NON-MEMBER of the Worker transfer set: it MUST NOT be
  transferred, so an off-thread round trip cannot observe or drop an override.
- FLAGS bit 4 BILLBOARD is RESERVED (no draw consumer in 2.0.0). Its public setter
  (setBillboard), the addNode({billboard}) init, and the Billboard arena tag are
  kept in lockstep so a D8 Sprites consumer can walk the set without a flags-word
  renumber. See LANES.md for the full FLAGS freeze table.

## createStage(ctx, opts) -> Stage

opts: { width, height, dpr, maxNodes, maxVerts, maxDrawFaces, maxClipVerts,
        camera, checked }
- checked (dev only, default false): forwards to lite-arena's checked Arena --
  idx() validates liveness/membership and join/joinN hand back a staleness-guarded
  plan that THROWS on a stale read or a set that is both required + excluded
  (surfaces a consumer interleaving its own arena joins with a lite-depth pass). The
  unchecked default path is byte-identical, so production frame() cost is unchanged.
- maxVerts = TOTAL projected vertices across all visible instances per frame
  (sphere(_,10,6) = 77 verts, box = 8). Undersizing silently drops geometry.
- maxDrawFaces = total draw-face budget per frame. A SHADOW-CASTING node counts
  TWICE: once for its own faces, once for the flat ground-shadow faces it emits
  (D5). Size for (visible faces + shadow-caster faces) or shadows fail closed
  (facesOverflowed) once the budget fills.
- maxClipVerts = per-FRAME screen-vertex scratch budget shared by the near-plane
  clip AND the D5 shadow pass (both store explicit-vertex polygons). Default 4096.
  This is NOT the per-face vertex cap: that is the fixed CLIP_CAP=16 constant.
- camera: { fov, near, far, ortho, orthoScale, theta, phi, radius,
  targetX/Y/Z }.

## Geometry (register with stage.geometry(g) -> id)

    geometry.box(w=1,h=1,d=1)              // 8 verts, 6 QUAD faces
    geometry.plane(w=1,d=1)                // 4 verts, 1 face
    geometry.sphere(r=0.5, segU=12, segV=8)
    geometry.cylinder(r=0.5, h=1, seg=16)
    geometry.cone(r=0.5, h=1, seg=16)
    geometry.polyline(points)              // flat xyz array; kind='stroke', F=0
    geometry.custom(verts, faces)          // verts flat xyz; faces = index loops
Geometry fields: V, F, verts(Float32), faceVertOffset(Uint32,len F+1),
faceVerts(Uint32), faceNormal(Float32), radius, kind ('fill'|'stroke').
Quads/n-gons first-class. Normals via Newell's method.

## Material (register with stage.material(m) -> id)

    material({ r=90,g=200,b=120, ambient=0.35, steps=64, stroke=null,
               lineWidth=2, fill=true })   // bakes a K-step hex ramp
    materialFromRamp(hexRamp, { stroke, lineWidth, fill })  // e.g. lite-hueforge scale
Per-frame shade is one LUT index, baked into the shade lane during collect and
read once by paint: lut[shade]. No per-frame string build, no per-face normal math
in the paint loop.
K CAP: steps (and a materialFromRamp ramp length) is capped at 256 -- the per-frame
shade lane is a Uint8Array, so an index must fit 0..255. A larger ramp THROWS at
creation (fail closed, did-you-mean hint) rather than silently wrapping to step 0.
fill=false: the face is NOT filled (honoured since v1.4.0; before, fill:false still
filled). stroke set: the face OUTLINE is stroked in the same style-run batch --
fill:false + stroke gives a wireframe; fill:true + stroke gives fill-then-outline.

## Nodes (Stage methods; h = generational NodeHandle)

    h = stage.addNode(geomId, matId, { x, y, z, layer, parent,
                                       pickable, castShadow, billboard })
    stage.setPosition(h, x, y, z)
    stage.setScale(h, x, y?, z?)           // uniform if y/z omitted
    stage.setQuaternion(h, x, y, z, w)
    stage.setEuler(h, ex, ey, ez)          // XYZ, radians
    stage.setParent(h, parentHandle)       // 0/undefined = root; cold topo rebuild
    stage.setLayer(h, 0..63)               // high bits of the sort key. 2.0.0
                                           // BREAKING: a layer outside 0..63 now
                                           // THROWS (fail-closed, did-you-mean),
                                           // was a silent & 63 wrap. addNode's
                                           // {layer} init fails closed the same way.
    stage.setDepthBias(h, bias)            // added to viewZ before quantize (popping fix)
    stage.setVisible(h, bool)
    stage.setPickable(h, bool)             // D5: bit + Pickable tag in lockstep
    stage.setCastShadow(h, bool)           // D5: bit + ShadowCaster tag in lockstep
    stage.setBillboard(h, bool)            // D5: bit + Billboard tag (tag reserved; see below)
    stage.setMaterialOverride(h, matId)    // D6.5: persistent per-node material; -1
                                           // restores the node's own material. COLD,
                                           // fail-closed: dead handle or unknown matId
                                           // throws (with the valid id range), never a
                                           // silent clamp. Shadow fills keep the stage shadow
                                           // material -- an override never leaks into
                                           // a caster's ground shadow.
    stage.remove(h)                        // generational: stale handle invalidates
    stage.resize(w, h, dpr?)
Stale handles after remove() are safe: isAlive(h) is false, never aliases a
recycled slot.

## Lifecycle (cold path; scene reload / capacity growth)

    stage.clear()             // remove all nodes in place, keep capacity/geometry/
                              // material/camera/arenas; 0 alloc; returns stage.
                              // EVERY handle minted before clear() is invalid after.
    stage.reserve(n)          // grow all node-capacity lanes to n; false if
                              // n<=capacity, true after grow; throws on bad arg.
    stage.remainingNodes      // getter: free node slots (capacity - live count)
    stage.structureEpoch      // getter: Uint32, bumped by addNode/remove/setParent/
                              // clear. Invalidation signal for cached dense indices.
A parent handle that is dead/recycled when topology rebuilds reparents its child
to ROOT and bumps stats.nodesOrphaned (fail closed, never inherits a stranger's
matrix). A parent CYCLE throws from the cold topo rebuild, naming both nodes.

## Frame + stats

    const s = stage.frame(dt);
    // s = { facesDrawn, facesCulled, nodesCulled, drawCalls,
    //       tTransform, tProject, tSort, tPaint,          (ms for the t* fields)
    //       nodesCulled,       // nodes rejected by EITHER the coarse depth/frustum
    //                          // reject OR the v1.5.0 per-node screen-space AABB
    //                          // cull. A screen-box-culled node runs ZERO face-loop
    //                          // iterations, so its faces are NOT in facesCulled --
    //                          // that is the v1.5.0 semantics shift (was: every
    //                          // off-screen face counted in facesCulled).
    //       facesOverflowed,   // nodes skipped by the vert/draw-face overflow door
    //       nodesInvalid,      // nodes rejected by the fail-closed collect door:
    //                          // a non-finite (NaN/Inf) pose lane, centroid, radius
    //                          // or bias -> whole node skipped, never laundered
    //       nodesNonUniform,   // drawn nodes with a non-uniform LOCAL scale (flag);
    //                          // inherited-only descendants are shaded via the
    //                          // inverse-transpose too but are not counted here
    //       nodesOrphaned,     // nodes whose dead parent forced a ROOT reparent
    //       nodesTotal,        // live node count this frame
    //       shadowFacesDrawn,  // D5: flat ground-shadow faces painted this frame,
    //                          // counted APART from facesDrawn so a caster is never
    //                          // double-counted (its own faces stay in facesDrawn)
    //       offthreadStalls,   // D6: monotonic RUN counter of frames SKIPPED because
    //                          // a bound Worker had not yet returned the transform
    //                          // buffers (fail-closed stall; canvas keeps last paint).
    //                          // Incremented on a stall, never reset in frame(). 0
    //                          // when no Worker is bound.
    //       facesClipped,      // D6.5: PER-FRAME (reset each frame() like facesDrawn):
    //                          // faces the near-plane clip pass actually emitted a
    //                          // clipped polygon for this frame. Distinct from
    //                          // facesCulled (whole-face near reject). 0 when
    //                          // clipNear is false or nothing straddles near.
    //       pickHits }         // D6.5: MONOTONIC (like offthreadStalls, never reset in
    //                          // frame()): successful pick() resolutions (a pick that
    //                          // returned 1) since stage creation. Picking is
    //                          // pointer-driven, not per-frame, so a running total
    //                          // maps; a missed pick does not increment it.

## Per-node screen cull + dirty-rect (v1.5.0)

Each visible node builds a screen-space AABB over its FRONT-OF-NEAR verts (z<=-near)
during projection. If that box misses the viewport the whole node is culled
(nodesCulled +1, zero face-loop work). Two deliberately OPPOSITE doors:
- face-bound NaN in the per-face viewport test -> the face is CULLED (fail CLOSED;
  losing a degenerate face is safe).
- an empty/non-finite node box (all verts behind near) -> the node is DRAWN, never
  node-culled (fail OPEN; a wrongly-fired geometry cull loses picture). Its faces
  are then rejected by the per-face near door, byte-identical to v1.4.0.

    stage.dirtyRect = true;     // OPT-IN (default false). When on, each drawn node's
                                // screen box is stored and merged once per frame.
                                // OFF => zero added hot cost (no nodeBox write, no
                                // merge). The screen-cull itself is ALWAYS on.
    stage.sceneBox              // getter: Float32Array[4] [minX,minY,maxX,maxY], the
                                // union of this frame's drawn node boxes (canonical
                                // empty box until dirtyRect is enabled + a frame runs)
    stage.prevSceneBox          // getter: the previous frame's union, for a redraw
                                // delta (repaint sceneBox U prevSceneBox)
Bounds are rounded OUTWARD to f32 so the stored box never clips the true box.
Grown in lockstep by stage.reserve(n).

## Near-plane clip (v1.6.0 / D4)

    stage.clipNear = true;      // ON by default. A face straddling the near plane is
                                // Sutherland-Hodgman-clipped against z=-near and drawn.
                                // Set false to restore v1.5.1 (a straddling face is
                                // near-culled whole). Cold straddle path only -- the
                                // fully-front fast path is byte-identical either way.
Per-face vertex cap is CLIP_CAP=16 (a >=16-vert face straddling near is rejected
whole, fail closed). Clip scratch is LAZY: allocated on the first straddle, so a
scene that never straddles keeps the smaller footprint. Budget is maxClipVerts.

## Screen-space picking (v1.6.0 / D4; post-projection, NOT a 3D raycast)

Picks read the per-node screen-box lane, so they REQUIRE the box lane populated:
either a bound spatial index (forces it on) or dirtyRect=true. Fail closed otherwise
(a stale lane would return a phantom hit).

    stage.pick(x, y, out)            // topmost node under a point. Returns 1 + writes
                                     // the dense index to out[0], or 0. Walks the
                                     // sorted draw list back-to-front (last painted =
                                     // nearest); with an index, queryPoint prunes to
                                     // broadphase candidates first.
    stage.pickRect(x0,y0,x1,y1,out)  // dense indices whose box overlaps the rect ->
                                     // out; returns count (clamped to out.length).
    stage.pickRay(p0x,p0y,p1x,p1y,out) // dense indices whose box the segment crosses
                                     // -> out; returns count. Non-finite ends -> 0.
    stage.nearest(x, y, radius)      // nearest node whose box is within radius px, or
                                     // -1. Squared-distance test, no Math.sqrt.
    stage.picked                     // last picked dense index (-1 = none)
    stage.onPick = (id, ev) => {}    // optional pick callback for the pointer plumbing
    stage.attachPointer(el)          // pointerdown/move/up -> pick(); returns stage
    stage.detachPointer(el)          // remove the listeners; returns stage
All pick paths are zero-alloc (caller-owned out + reused scratch).

    stage.useSpatialIndex(tree, { margin })  // DI-bind a DynamicBVH2D-shaped tree
                                     // (lite-bvh, never a runtime dep). Forces the box
                                     // lane on; the tree is clear()+insertLeaves-rebuilt
                                     // each frame from the node boxes (zero-alloc).
                                     // margin: non-negative fatten. Returns stage.
    stage.dropSpatialIndex()         // unbind; pick reverts to the dirtyRect fallback.

## Layers: tags, ground shadows, pickSet (D5)

D5 adds three flag-backed MEMBERSHIP tags plus a per-frame derived Culled set, all
lite-arena registerTag() sets. Each of the three mirrors a FLAGS bit and is kept in
lockstep on addNode / the set* setters / remove / clear -- the bit stays the hot
per-node compare in collect, the tag turns an O(nodes) secondary scan into an
O(members) walk for the cold passes. Pickable feeds pickSet, ShadowCaster feeds the
shadow pass; Billboard's bit/tag are maintained but have no internal draw consumer
yet -- RESERVED for a future billboard pass (FLAGS D-14: every FLAGS bit is either
consumed by code or reserved with a dated milestone).

    // shadows: register a dark material, tag casters, set the stage shadow material
    const shadowMat = stage.material(material({ r: 20, g: 20, b: 24 }));
    stage.setShadowMaterial(shadowMat);   // -1 (default) disables -> NO shadow pass
    stage.setCastShadow(h, true);         // or addNode(..., { castShadow: true })
Each non-culled ShadowCaster's faces are flatten-projected onto the world plane y=0
along stage.light, then appended to the SAME draw list as DRAW_SHADOW polygons.
Ordering (so the caster paints over its own shadow, no real-face key changed):
- caster at layer L >= 1: shadow goes to layer L-1 -- the layer bits alone put it
  strictly under the caster regardless of depth; within layer L-1 shadows sort by
  their ground-projected depth.
- caster at layer 0 (default): there is no layer below, so every layer-0 shadow is
  keyed at the caster's FARTHEST view-space extent (bounding-sphere far point) minus
  one depth unit -- strictly below every one of that caster's real face keys (a face
  centroid is never farther than the bounding sphere; quantize is monotonic). It thus
  sorts at (just below) the caster's far depth within layer 0.
shadowFacesDrawn counts shadow faces apart from facesDrawn. Fail closed: a light parallel to the ground casts no
shadow; a culled or invisible caster casts nothing. Flatten-matrix onto ONE plane --
NOT shadow maps, NOT soft shadows. With NO shadow material set, the draw output is
byte-identical to 1.6.0 (matOverride[e] === the node material for every fill).

    stage.pickSet(out)               // pickable, non-culled dense indices -> out;
                                     // returns count (clamped to out.length). Bounds
                                     // a pick broadphase to the pickable set via
                                     // joinN([Pickable],[Culled]). Call after frame();
                                     // Culled reflects the most recent frame. 0 alloc.

PLAN-REUSE CONTRACT (lite-arena shared scratch): lite-depth calls arena.joinN at
most ONCE per pass (shadow pass; pickSet) and consumes the reused plan IMMEDIATELY,
never retaining it. A consumer that calls arena.joinN on the SAME arena mid-frame
(between lite-depth reading the plan and finishing the pass) invalidates lite-depth's
plan -- so do not interleave your own joins with a frame in progress. The plan and
its others/excl arrays are arena-owned reused scratch; loop to count/exclCount,
never .length.

## Camera

    updateCamera(stage.camera)             // cold; rebuild world->view after mutating
    stage.camera.theta/phi/radius/tx/ty/tz/fov/near/far/ortho/orthoScale
Interaction (drag/pinch/inertia) is NOT in core — wire pointer events to
theta/phi/radius + updateCamera yourself, or use a companion driver.
stage.view2d (Float64Array[6] or null): optional per-frame setTransform — the
2D screen-space camera composition hook over the 3D scene.

## lite-signal DI (cold path)

    import { effect } from '@zakkster/lite-signal';
    stage.useSignals({ effect });
    stage.bind(h, 'position'|'scale'|'quaternion', () => signalGetter());
Effect writes lanes + marks dirty on the cold path; frame loop only reads lanes.

## Off-thread transform (D6; opt-in DI)

    import { Worker } from 'node:worker_threads';            // or a browser Worker
    const worker = new Worker(new URL('@zakkster/lite-depth/DepthWorker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' });
    stage.useWorker(worker);   // bind; returns stage. useWorker(null) unbinds.

Moves the transform pass (compose TRS -> local -> world in topo order) off the main
thread via lite-arena's detach/rebind transferable round-trip. DepthWorker.js reuses
Depth.js's mathKernels (composeTRS/mulAffine) and FLAGS -- it does not reimplement the
math. Cold DI, mirrors useSignals(); default absent -> the frame body is byte-identical
to the on-thread v1.6.0 path (one boolean gate at the top of frame() dispatches to a
separate, never-inlined _offthreadFrame).

Model (one-frame-latency pipeline, transfer is the fence -- one thread owns a buffer at
a time; plain ArrayBuffer only, NO SharedArrayBuffer / atomics):
  - Each frame projects the world matrices the Worker composed from the PREVIOUS send,
    then transfers the current lanes out for the NEXT compose.
  - PER-FRAME transfer set (ONE postMessage each direction): the 10 pose lanes
    (px,py,pz,qx,qy,qz,qw,sx,sy,sz) + `flags` + the 12 world-matrix lanes (m0..m11),
    plus the stage-owned worldNonUnif buffer. `flags` is transferred so the Worker
    propagates the WORLD non-uniform bit (worldNonUnif) in topo order EXACTLY as the
    on-thread loop does -- giving f64-EXACT shade parity across both backends,
    including a non-uniform node and any child of a non-uniform parent.
  - topo / parentDense are STRUCTURAL: the main thread keeps its own home copies and
    sends the Worker COPIES once on bind, re-syncing only when stage.structureEpoch
    changes -- never out-and-back per frame.

Fail-closed (frame() NEVER reads a detached lane):
  - Bootstrap: until one real reply has rebound composed matrices, frame 1 SENDS the
    poses but SKIPS the project (offthreadStalls++) -- it never paints zero matrices.
  - In-flight stall: if a frame runs while the lanes are still out at the Worker, the
    WHOLE frame is skipped (offthreadStalls++); the canvas keeps its last paint.
  - Unbind mid-flight: useWorker(null) while a send is in flight DEFERS -- the
    off-thread path keeps stalling until the reply rebinds every lane, then the return
    handler completes the switch to main-thread mode.
  - A corrupt Worker reply is a loud crash: nodes.rebind validates every buffer
    (type + exact capacity size) before repointing any.
  - The cold pose setters (setPosition/setScale/setQuaternion/setEuler) THROW while a
    send is in flight (pose lanes detached) rather than silently drop the write; issue
    them while lanes are home (post-reply, or before useWorker()/after useWorker(null)).
  - If the bound Worker dies or never replies while a send is in flight, useWorker(null)
    cannot complete: frame() stalls (offthreadStalls climbs) indefinitely, with no
    lane-recovery API -- a deliberate liveness/safety tradeoff. Never terminate a Worker
    while a send is outstanding.

Allocation: the main-thread frame BODY (project/collect/sort/paint + the send leg) is
0 B/op. The return-leg rebind re-views the transferred-back buffers -- young-gen only,
gated at 0 major GC over 20000 frames; it is not a 0-byte op. The Worker's transform
runs on its own thread/heap and never touches the main-thread budget.

## Light

stage.light is a normalized Float64Array[3] directional light. Flat per-face
shading = clamp(dot(worldNormal, light), 0, 1), ambient floor from the material.
worldNormal is derived from the node's WORLD matrix (the same transform the
geometry is drawn from), NOT the local quaternion -- so a child of a rotated /
scaled parent is lit correctly (fixed in v1.4.0; before, hierarchical scenes were
mis-lit). Mechanics, computed ONCE per node in collect:
  - Uniform world basis (a similarity): the light is back-rotated into the
    geometry's local frame, and each face is a single sqrt-free dot with its
    precomputed local normal.
  - Non-uniform world basis: the normal matrix (inverse-transpose / adjugate of the
    world upper-3x3) is built once, and each face does normal*matrix, normalize,
    dot. This path is selected by a per-node WORLD non-uniform bit that propagates
    down the hierarchy in topo order (own non-uniform local scale OR any
    non-uniform ancestor -- rotation is a similarity and does NOT taint), so an
    inherited non-uniform scale is handled correctly.
The shade is baked into a per-draw shade lane during collect; paint() reads that
lane -- no per-face normal math. stats.nodesNonUniform counts drawn nodes with a
non-uniform LOCAL scale (the flag); inherited-only descendants are shaded via the
inverse-transpose but are not themselves counted.

## Math kernels (out-param, no classes; affine 3x4 row-major)

    mathKernels.composeTRS(out12, tx,ty,tz, qx,qy,qz,qw, sx,sy,sz)
    mathKernels.mulAffine(out12, A12, B12)     // out = A*B (parent*local)
    mathKernels.quatRotate(out3, qx,qy,qz,qw, vx,vy,vz)

## Gotchas

- maxVerts/maxDrawFaces must cover the worst-case VISIBLE scene; sphere verts are
  (segU+1)*(segV+1). Undersizing is now fail-closed: an over-budget node is
  SKIPPED whole (two integer compares per node) and stats.facesOverflowed counts
  it -- no out-of-range write, no partial face. Size up when facesOverflowed > 0.
- Back-face cull uses screen winding; DOUBLE_SIDED flag disables it per node.
- Depth key: far->0, near->DEPTH_MAX. depthBias shifts a node earlier/later.
- Zero-alloc applies to frame(); creation/reconfiguration is cold and may allocate.
- Verifying zero-GC: use @zakkster/lite-gc-profiler and await gc.settle() before
  reading the summary — the perf_hooks GC observer delivers asynchronously.

## Motion subpath — @zakkster/lite-depth/motion (v1.3.0)

Optional animation layer. Thin composer over the stack: lite-clock (time base),
lite-keyframe KeyframePool (scalar channels), lite-ease (easing bank). Adds only
quaternion slerp tracks + a clip table bound to node lanes. Optional peer deps:
lite-clock, lite-keyframe, lite-ease (install only if you import this subpath).

    import { createMixer } from '@zakkster/lite-depth/motion';
    const mixer = createMixer(stage, { clock, maxClips, maxKeys, easings });

createMixer(stage, opts) -> Mixer
  opts: { clock?, maxClips=256, maxKeys=8, maxQuatKeys=8, easings? }
  clock: a lite-clock (duck-typed via clock.simTime). Omit for standalone dt mode.
  easings: array of lite-ease function names; index 0 should be 'linear'. Names
           become the ids used by the `ease` argument on *Key calls.

mixer.clip(nodeHandle) -> Clip   (chainable; all keys take time in SECONDS)
  clip.posKey(t, x, y, z, ease?)
  clip.scaleKey(t, s, ease?)                 // uniform
  clip.scaleKey(t, x, y, z, ease?)           // per-axis (string in an axis slot = ease)
  clip.biasKey(t, v, ease?)                  // depth-bias
  clip.quatKey(t, x, y, z, w, ease?)         // slerp (nlerp fast path at dot>0.9995)
  clip.quatEuler(t, ex, ey, ez, ease?)       // XYZ Euler radians -> quat
  clip.play({ duration?, loop?, timescale?, start? })
       duration inferred from last key if omitted; loop: 'loop'|'pingpong'|number
  clip.pause() / resume() / stop() / seek(localSeconds)
  clip.done / clip.playing

mixer.update(dt)  // standalone: advance internal time by dt, then apply
mixer.sync()      // clock mode: apply at clock.simTime (call after clock.advance)
mixer.time / mixer.clipCount
exports: createMixer, ONCE, LOOP, PINGPONG, version

Time base / determinism: in clock mode global pause/seek/replay live on the clock;
fixed advance(dt) gives golden-frame determinism (byte-identical lanes). The update
path is allocation-free (channels write straight into Float64 lanes; 0 GC over
20000 ops, gated on bytes/op not scavenge count).

Motion gotchas:
- Keyframe times are ABSOLUTE seconds within the clip, not normalized [0,1].
- scaleKey uniform-with-ease: pass the ease as the 3rd arg, e.g.
  scaleKey(t, 1.5, 'easeOutCubic') — a string in an axis slot is read as the ease.
- Quaternion keyframe values are stored Float32 (slerp math is bit-exact; the
  ~1e-7 delta vs a Float64 reference is storage precision, not error).

## Test / bench

    npm test          # node:test (20 files: core/pipeline/zero-GC 01/03/04/10-23,
                      # motion 06/07/09); the zero-GC tests skip without --expose-gc
    npm run test:gc   # --expose-gc; zero-GC contracts engage
    npm run torture   # node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs -> prints "ok" (zero-GC gate)
    npm run bench     # vs Zdog + throughput sweep
